nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Markov decision process with finitely many states, real rewards and stochastic transition probabilities, and let $0 \le \gamma < 1$. For every deterministic stationary policy $\mu$, the SSP value of $\mu$ in the associated SSP is the discounted value of the policy $\mu$ in $M$. Results for SSP problems therefore specialize to discounted problems.
nodes.title: The SSP value of a discounted MDP's policy is its discounted value

For a proper policy of a substochastic MDP the limit exists, is the unique fixed point of $T_\mu$, and equals the total expected reward until termination $\sum_{k \ge 0} P_\mu^k r_\mu$.…

nodes.summary: A Markov decision process with real transition probabilities $p(s, a, s')$ among its nonterminal states is substochastic if $p(s, a, s') \ge 0$ for all $s, a, s'$ and $\sum_{s'} p(s, a, s') \le 1$ for all $s, a$. The missing mass $1 - \sum_{s'} p(s, a, s')$ is the probability of moving from $s$ under action $a$ to the termination state, which is cost-free and absorbing and is not modelled explicitly.
nodes.title: Substochastic transitions

For every $J : S \to \mathbb{R}$, the iterates $T_\mu^k J$ of the undiscounted Bellman operator of $\mu$ converge, as $k \to \infty$, to the value of $\mu$.

nodes.title: The SSP of a discounted MDP is substochastic

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Markov decision process with real rewards $r(s,a)$ and transition probabilities $p(s,a,s')$, and let $\gamma$ be a discount factor. The associated stochastic shortest path problem has the same states, actions and rewards, and transition probabilities $\gamma\, p(s,a,s')$ among the states: at every stage the system terminates with probability $1 - \gamma$ and otherwise moves as in $M$.
nodes.title: A discounted MDP as a stochastic shortest path problem

nodes.summary: For a Markov decision process with finitely many states and substochastic transitions, a deterministic stationary policy $\mu$ and every $k \ge 0$, the entries of $P_\mu^k$ are nonnegative and each row of $P_\mu^k$ sums to at most $1$.
nodes.title: Powers of a substochastic matrix are substochastic

nodes.summary: For a Markov decision process with states $S$ and a deterministic stationary policy $\mu : S \to A$, the transition matrix of $\mu$ is the $S \times S$ matrix $P_\mu$ with entries $P_\mu(s, s') = p(s, \mu(s), s')$. In a stochastic shortest path problem $S$ is the set of nonterminal states and $P_\mu$ is substochastic.
